system.summary: Homophonic letter cipher in graphic signs, two or three signs per common letter, with a dozen syllable and word signs (et, nt, st, de, ou, ns, car, pour, Allemagne, l'Empereur).

diacritics.note: A dot under the m sign makes st.

system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's reconstructed table for the Monluc/Lansac ciphers (henryiii_Lansac.png), shifted by one letter from m onward; compared, corrected, not used as the key.
system.notes: 47 signs met in f. 124 and the glossed siblings; commas, points and short bars separate words. Three signs (4, the n-bar, 3-hook) unread in session 1, some fixed in session 2.

solution.what: Tomokiyo's table and Noailles 1867 checked; the 26 April letter is in neither, Tomokiyo gives no reading.
Fetched the Gallica IIIF microfilm scans of ff. 121-164 with back-off.
Transcribed 741 tokens from f. 124, f. 154, f. 154v l. 1 and f. 156.
Glossed sibling f. 154v l. 1 'car je n'ay pas cinquante' fixed 12 signs and showed Tomokiyo's row shifted.
Passage 2 of f. 124 read by hand against its gloss 'pour le moins esté retenu'.
Pinned 5-gram annealer over the whole transcription filled the free signs.
Shuffled-token and blind runs: shuffled score far worse; blind run finds a better-scoring wrong key (6 of 21 crib letters).
Lattice beam decode of both f. 124 passages; 96 of 100 signs read.
Key carried to ff. 160, 164, 174; read in substance, short runs open.
Readings agree with the surviving gloss fragments on every leaf.
Fetched ff. 154r-v, 156r-157v at full size and canvases 330-358 at 600/1400 px from Gallica IIIF to locate ff. 182 ff.

Checked the 9 May letters ff. 182 (Anjou), 184 (Catherine), 186 (Brulart), 188 (Lanssac pere): all in clear, no cipher, no marginal decipherment; the session-2 expectation that they were in the key was wrong.
Re-transcribed f. 154r (19 lines) and f. 154v (two blocks) with word groups aligned to the plaintext (ct_f154.txt, ct_f154v.txt), 679 tokens.
Re-transcribed f. 156r (two blocks, 316 tokens) and a first pass of f. 156v (515 tokens) at reduced scale.
Outer-margin glosses of f. 154v and f. 156v, which survive whole, used as cribs; inner-margin fragments of ff. 154r/156r used as checks.
Session 1-2 key applied unchanged; read most of ff. 154r and 156r at once.
Key extended from context and glosses: Gf = me, Ng = qu, Nb = il, obul = bien, Pi2 = x/y, Co = o, vo = l'Empereur, 5 = n, M/Mx/sq = x, 4 = b confirmed.
Tried the session-1 value N = p and session-2 N = a for the barred N on ff. 154-156: neither fits; there it reads il.
Tried to read the 11-sign group after 'de la Valaquie' (f. 154r l. 15) and the 4-sign group after 'vaivode' with the key and variant values; no French word.
Measured share of tokens read as sense: f. 154r 92.5%, f. 154v 92.0%, f. 156r 97.2%, f. 156v 67.2% (first pass).
Raw first-value decode vs three shufflings under fr-1600-letters (no spaces): -1.93 to -3.00 per char vs -4.4 to -4.7.
Readings agree with every surviving gloss fragment of ff. 154r and 156r and with the full verso glosses.
f. 156v re-transcribed line by line at full scale (pass 2): 645 tokens against 515 in pass 1; whole lines had been merged or skipped at reduced scale.

Outer-margin decipherment of f. 156v aligned line by line with the pass-2 tokens; read 'voient enclos de deux si puissantz roys comme ilz seront', 'demanderont qu'il ameine quatre mil gascons', 'faire mettre en ordre les galleres pour pouvoir servir', 'toute la noblesse crie pour avoir ung roy'.
New values from pass 2: Mu = u/qu (Tomokiyo's u), Ne = est, Gq = qu, Bf = f ('mon frere' for the gloss 'monsieur'), qq = par; Gf generalised to me/nous.
Tried to read the gloss 'cependant', 'estoit ennemy', 'ensemble afin', 'de ceste nation' sign by sign on f. 156v: the cipher groups do not match; the gloss paraphrases at these points.
Rechecked f. 124 'despuis' with the barred N = il of ff. 154-156: gives 'desiluis', no French; the f. 124 sign is a different barred-N form; 'despuis' (N = p) stands.
Final retry of every unread group on ff. 154r, 154v, 156r with the extended key: f. 154r 92.5% -> 96.7% (nous x2, qui, qui est, ameine); f. 154v and 156r unchanged.
Raw first-value decode vs shuffles after pass 2: f. 154r -2.25, f. 156v -2.60 per char vs -4.4 to -4.7 shuffled.
Looked for other photographs of fr. 4735: Gallica SRU returns one digitisation (btv1b9060724s, microfilm), no colour scan; Tomokiyo's cryptiana page has no image of the leaves.
Compared key.tsv with Tomokiyo's current table (henryiii_Lansac.png): adopted st = stacked 8, il = barred N, nous = barred Gamma, q = 6, t = footed Pi.
f. 154v l. 7 past the end of the gloss read 'le[s] nostre si inferieur'; gutter signs of ll. 1 and 5 identified (e of escus, s of longtemps).

f. 156v l. 10-11 re-read with st = stacked 8: 'se monstrent estre ennemis jurez de ... France et specialement de Monseigneur, et lesquelz [so]nt extremement marrys'; the decipherer's 'si monsieur estoit ennemy' is a misreading; pass 2's 'mon frere' withdrawn.
f. 156v: 'à faire estat que', 'il n'y en a que quatre con[tr]e nous', 'et nommement veule[nt]', 'empeschée', 'ca[r]' read with the gloss sense and sign values.
Barred-N forms separated on all pages: barred N = il throughout ff. 154-156; f. 124 looped form stays p (despuis); f. 160 'N = a' was a misread tall T (re-read on c307).
Measured after pass 3: f. 154r 96.7%, f. 154v 99.1%, f. 156r 97.2%, f. 156v 95.2%; letter to Anjou 97.5%, letter to Catherine 95.8%, four pages 96.5% (1581/1638).
Raw first-value decode vs shuffles after pass 3: -2.25, -2.20, -1.93, -2.49 per char vs -4.4 to -4.7.
ff. 160, 164, 174 re-transcribed word-aligned at full scale (ct_f160/164/174.txt); f. 164's first cipher line had been skipped in session 2.

f. 164 open runs read with the extended key and Tomokiyo's pour/par/et: 'en toutes sortes pour venir a vostre desir', 'car si jusques cy ... a despendu trente mil escus en ceste negotiation', 'et n'y faict toutefois riens qui vaille pour soy; mais seulement', 'vostre desseing'.
f. 174 run after 'Moscovite' was a misdivision; f. 160 'et' and 'par' confirmed as Tomokiyo's word signs; both letters read in full.
Tried to read the f. 164 word sign Mc (subject of 'a despendu trente mil escus'): not in the key or Tomokiyo's table, gloss cut; left open.
Raw first-value decode vs shuffles for ff. 160/164/174: -2.26/-2.11/-1.94 per char vs -3.8 to -4.3.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 1842 tokens, 73 types, fr-1600-letters order 4: reading -1.997 per letter; random keys -4.815 (z 8.3); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.912 (mean -2.947, z 46.2); annealer on the real text -2.06. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): f. 124 (ct_f124.txt, reading.txt), ff. 154r-v (ct_f154/ct_f154v, read_f154.md), ff. 156-157 (ct_f156/ct_f156v, read_f156.md), ff. 160/164/174 (ct_*, read_f160_f174.md); key key.tsv.

texts.label: f. 124, to Charles IX, Warsaw, 26 April 1573 (no. 51)
texts.summary: Lanssac tells Charles IX that the obstacles in Thuringia, Meissen and the Mark of Brandenburg delayed him so that he reached Poland (Mezeritz) only on 25 February, and that without the escort of the King's pensioners Alexander von Miltitz and George Luelz he would at the least have been detained; the ciphered passages hide the dangers Frenchmen met in Germany. The rest, in clear, refers to his recueil on Polish affairs.

texts.label: ff. 154r-v, to the duc d'Anjou, Warsaw, 24 April 1573 (no. 60)
texts.summary: On the eve of the Polish election, Lanssac reports to Anjou that the Lithuanian chiefs have promised their vote to him, which with the party already won should put the crown on his head, unless the Grand Seigneur's recommendation of him, made with ruse through the voivode of Wallachia, brings some unexpected change.

texts.label: ff. 156-157, to Catherine de Médicis, Warsaw, 24 April 1573 (no. 61)
texts.summary: Lanssac tells Catherine that matters stand so that by next Monday she should be mother of the two greatest kings in the world, barring a change of minds, and fears that the Emperor might surprise them and that the King of Denmark, bending to his will, might give them much trouble on that side because of the strait, not half a league wide. The end of the letter (f. 157r) is in clear.

texts.label: ff. 160, 164, 174, to Charles IX and Anjou, 1 and 9 May 1573 (nos. 63, 65, 70)
texts.summary: f. 160: the Polish nation is as venal as its German neighbours. f. 164: the Emperor has spent more than 300,000 écus in the negotiation against 30,000 on the other side and achieves nothing but to trouble Anjou's design. f. 174 (Płock, 9 May), announcing the election: it succeeded against the will of the Grand Seigneur, the Emperor, the princes of the Empire, the King of Spain, the Muscovite and the King of Sweden.
